h: Arthur, amphitheatres and a bigger day out
p: Caerleon has legends as well as Romans. In the twelfth century, Geoffrey of Monmouth placed King Arthur's court here, and for centuries locals linked the grassy bowl of the amphitheatre with the Round Table. It's pure legend, of course, but it adds a lovely layer of story when you're standing in the middle of the arena.

Give yourself at least half a day to do the museum and the Roman sites justice. The amphitheatre and the barracks are free and open-air, so they're best on a dry day, while the Roman Baths Museum, cared for by Cadw, gives you the cover of a roof if the weather turns. Wear comfortable shoes, because the sites are spread around the village and you'll be walking between them.
The village itself is a pleasant spot with pubs and cafés, and there's a nice stroll down by the River Usk, which once brought supplies to the legion. It makes a great stop for lunch between sites.

Newport is just down the road and has more to add to your trip. Tredegar House, a grand seventeenth-century mansion run by the National Trust, has gardens and parkland to explore. Out by the Severn Estuary, Newport Wetlands is a peaceful place for a walk among reedbeds with excellent birdwatching. Combine the Romans in the morning with wetlands or a stately home in the afternoon and you've got a proper south Wales day out.
